blocks.prompt: 16. If \(\frac{1}{a + b},\ \frac{1}{c + a},\ \frac{1}{b + c}\) are in A.P. then show that \(a^2,\ b^2,\ c^2\) are in A.P.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh proof (saabit karne) ka sawal hai. Humein ek baat di gayi hai aur us se doosri baat tak pahunchna hai.
Diya kya hai? Teen fractions A.P. mein hain.
Saabit kya karna hai? \(a^2,\ b^2,\ c^2\) A.P. mein hain, yani \(b^2 - a^2 = c^2 - b^2\).
Rule kaunsa? Teen cheezein A.P. mein tab hoti hain jab doosri − pehli = teesri − doosri.
Plan: fractions par yeh shart likhna, dono taraf simplify karna, phir cross-multiply.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\frac{1}{a + b},\ \frac{1}{c + a},\ \frac{1}{b + c}\) A.P. mein hain (yani \(a + b,\ b + c,\ c + a\) zero nahi).
Saabit karna hai: \(a^2,\ b^2,\ c^2\) A.P. mein hain, yani \(b^2 - a^2 = c^2 - b^2\).
Tareeqa: Common difference barabar hone wali shart lagayenge: doosri − pehli = teesri − doosri. Har taraf do fractions ka farq lenge; numerators mein cheezein cancel ho kar bohat simple ho jati hain. Yeh tareeqa \(\frac{2}{c + a} = \frac{1}{a + b} + \frac{1}{b + c}\) se zyada aasaan hai kyunke lambi expansion se bach jate hain.

A.P. ki shart likhein
\[\dfrac{1}{c + a} - \dfrac{1}{a + b}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{b + c} - \dfrac{1}{c + a}\]
Kyun: A.P. mein har do saath wali terms ka farq ek jaisa hota hai. Pehla farq (doosri − pehli) aur doosra farq (teesri − doosri) barabar rakh diye.

Left side simplify karein
\[\dfrac{(a + b) - (c + a)}{(c + a)(a + b)}\]
\[= \dfrac{b - c}{(c + a)(a + b)}\]
Kyun: Do fractions minus karne ke liye common denominator \((c + a)(a + b)\) liya. Upar \((a + b) - (c + a)\) mein \(a\) cancel ho gaya aur \(b - c\) bacha.
Dhyan dein: Bracket hatate waqt \(-(c + a) = -c - a\); dono signs badalte hain.

Right side simplify karein
\[\dfrac{(c + a) - (b + c)}{(b + c)(c + a)}\]
\[= \dfrac{a - b}{(b + c)(c + a)}\]
Kyun: Wohi kaam: common denominator \((b + c)(c + a)\), aur upar \(c\) cancel ho kar \(a - b\) bacha.

Barabar rakh kar \((c + a)\) cancel karein
\[\dfrac{b - c}{a + b} = \dfrac{a - b}{b + c}\]
Kyun: Dono taraf denominator mein \((c + a)\) hai. Dono sides ko \((c + a)\) se multiply kiya to woh dono taraf se hat gaya. (Yeh jaiz hai kyunke \(c + a \ne 0\).)

Cross-multiply karein
\[(b - c)(b + c) = (a - b)(a + b)\]
\[b^2 - c^2 = a^2 - b^2\]
Kyun: Cross-multiply: left ka numerator right ke denominator se aur right ka numerator left ke denominator se. Phir dono taraf "difference of squares" \((x - y)(x + y) = x^2 - y^2\) lagaya. Yahi woh jagah hai jahan squares paida hue.

Tarteeb badlein
\[b^2 - a^2 = c^2 - b^2\]
Kyun: \(a^2\) ko left aur \(c^2\) ko right le gaye: dono taraf \(c^2\) jama aur \(a^2\) minus kiya. Ab yeh bilkul A.P. ki shart ki shakal mein hai. Isi ko \(2b^2 = a^2 + c^2\) bhi likh sakte hain (beech wali term dono kinaron ka average).

Nateeja aur tasdeeq
\(a^2,\ b^2,\ c^2\) mein saath wali terms ka farq barabar hai, is liye yeh A.P. mein hain.
Numbers se check: \(a = 1,\ b = 5,\ c = 7\) se \(1, 25, 49\) (farq 24), aur fractions \(\frac{1}{6}, \frac{1}{8}, \frac{1}{12}\): \(\frac{1}{8} - \frac{1}{6} = -\frac{1}{24} = \frac{1}{12} - \frac{1}{8}\) \(\checkmark\)
Kyun: Proof ke baad ek numerical misaal se dekh lena achha hai ke baat waqai sahi hai: yahan fractions bhi A.P. mein hain aur squares bhi.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(b^2 - a^2 = c^2 - b^2\), is liye \(a^2,\ b^2,\ c^2\) A.P. mein hain.
